note.text: A utility table can illustrate the relationship between total and marginal utility for one consumer in fixed circumstances. The figures are hypothetical. Read units in order. For an extra unit, subtract the previous total utility from the new total. Total utility rises when marginal utility is positive, stays unchanged when it is zero and falls when it is negative. A table can illustrate diminishing marginal utility without claiming that satisfaction is directly measurable in everyday life.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Ngozi records an imagined example for portions of a snack. Each additional portion may add less satisfaction. Her exercise book needs separate columns for number consumed, total utility and marginal utility. Using one person's assumed values avoids pretending to compare different people's satisfaction. The practical asks you to calculate and interpret the differences, not to eat until uncomfortable.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Copy the hypothetical totals, compute consecutive differences and label the columns. When an increase becomes smaller, say marginal utility is diminishing; do not say total utility has fallen unless the difference is negative. Check each row against the preceding row rather than against zero.
